newsitem.title: UK: Dollar/mark keeps to session lows in late Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/mark keeps to session lows in late Europe.

text.p: The dollar was trading near its session lows against the mark in late European trade, pushed lower by a widening U.S. trade gap and signs of growing business activity in Germany.

"This was an exaggerated reaction to the trade figures with the bulk of the increase coming from higher oil prices," said Julian Jessop, chief European economist at Nikko Europe. "There was already an impact from the strong German Ifo survey."
The U.S. September trade deficit rose 10.1 percent to $11.34 billion from a forecast $9.5 billion shortfall. The August figure was revised down to $10.3 billion from $10.8 billion.
Earlier, the German research institute Ifo's business climate index for October rose to 97.4 from 95.7 previously. Analysts were expecting an increase to around 96.0.
"The German data has cut the chances of a Bundesbank easing near-term but talk of a U.S. rate hike is just too vague right now to give the dollar any lift," said one U.S. bank dealer.
The dollar against the mark was trading at 1.4960/66 at 1616 GMT from a session high of 1.5060 marks and 1.5036/45 Tuesday.
Dealers were cautious of the dollar below 1.50, mindful of last week's verbal dollar support from the Bundesbank when the dollar dipped as low as 1.4885 marks.

There was some wariness that the Bundesbank might again repeat its desire for a stronger dollar if the dollar slips too far below 1.50 marks. And with little on the data front for the rest of this week, official comments could be the only driving force for the dollar.
"The next dollar move will not probably come until the Bundesbank comes out again and says it wants a stronger dollar," said Nikko's Jessop. "The next move will depend on official comments."
Against the yen, the dollar was steady, trading at 111.15/25 after dipping briefly below 111 yen after the U.S. trade data.

Dollar/yen kept largely to fairly narrow ranges throughout the European session after being pushed lower overnight by seemingly conflicting comments from Japanese officials about interest rates and the strength of the economy.
Dealers said ongoing rumours of Japan's Tankan quarterly survey next week were also keeping the market nervous with the bias towards further dollar weakness.
"Rumours are typical ahead of the Tankan and tend to weigh on the dollar, but the 111 yen level is providing a good base," said the U.S. bank dealer.
Elsewhere, profit-taking and the dollar's afternoon slip against the mark knocked sterling off fresh four-year highs against the dollar and 30-month highs versus the mark.
Talk of higher UK interest rates continued to fuel sterling strength after a 10.3 percent rise in UK October M4 money supply and a 0.3 percent rise in October retail sales.
The pound stood at $1.6782/92 after touching a peak of $1.6820 in earlier trade. Against the mark, it stood at 2.5093/04 from a session high of 2.5260 marks.
